text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government and the country's power utility NamPower said the proposed Epupa hydropower project on Namibia's northern Cunene river is necessary for local development. The Himba community in the area of the planned dam site say however the project will flood pastures and ancestral graves.
- Namibia's fisheries ministry said South Africa and France have claimed that Namibian vessels are fishing illegally outside the country's 200 mile Exclusive Economic Zone.

- Deputy Minister of Mines and Energy, Jesaya Nyamu, told a public meeting at the weekend that the issue of the proposed Epupa power project was not whether to build a dam but which site should be chosen.
- Public drought assistance is being phased out after good rain this year, permanent secretary of the agriculture, water and rural development ministry Vaino Shivute said.
